topic: AI growth and PFAS cooling risks
angle: Chasing AI capacity without a sustainability plan is a future balance-sheet problem, not just a PR one.
sourceTitle: Data centers are swapping water for forever chemicals to keep AI cool
linkedinPost:
AI capacity isn’t free—someone is paying the environmental bill.

Fortune reports data centers are turning to PFAS-based cooling to cut water use. Short-term win on one metric; long-term risk on many others: regulation, remediation costs, supply dependency, and brand trust.

From the enterprise side, I’ve seen AI roadmaps that meticulously model GPU costs but treat sustainability as a footnote. That’s a CFO mistake. If PFAS becomes your cooling strategy, you’ve effectively taken on contingent liabilities and vendor concentration risk you need to price into TCO.

A practical approach:
- Add “sustainability-adjusted TCO” to every AI capacity decision—include regulatory scenarios.
- Plan for dual-path cooling (water-efficient + non-PFAS) to avoid lock-in.
- Tie model efficiency targets to infra externalities, not just cloud bills.

AI scale can drive real value, but only if you can keep the lights (and the reputation) on.

Is sustainability already in your AI business case model, or is it still a paragraph at the end? #AIStrategy #DigitalTransformation #EnterpriseAI
